lines.text: What if one warm meal kept you in a place you were never meant to stay?
A tired rabbit steps inside an old roadside inn, shivering from the winter storm.
The fox behind the counter slides over hot stew: 'Eat up, kid. First bowl is free.'
The rabbit clutches his packed bag: 'I should keep moving. My train leaves tonight.'
'The tracks are frozen,' the fox purrs with a wink. 'Just stay until morning.'
He stayed that morning. And the next. And twenty years vanished in the dark.
A cold highway diner under buzzing fluorescent tubes. An older rabbit wipes the counter.
Out on the rusted platform, the midnight train pulls away, disappearing into the fog.
Three in the morning. In shaking paws, he unfolds the ticket he never used.
Suddenly, you snap back to the warm tavern. The stew is hot. Your bag is packed.
The fox smiles: 'One more night?' You grab your coat and walk into the snow.
